correctness.rationale: For generic s>0 write a_i=|u_i| and k=#(a_i<s). Every (j+1)-simplex face of the cross-polytope cuts the plane in a j-face iff its signed vertex heights straddle s. For an m=j+2 coordinate set with q coordinates below s, count 2^m-2^q-1_{q=0}, producing exactly the displayed F_{d,j}(k). The vertex formula 2[binom(d,2)-binom(k,2)] proves d-1 distinct vectors (k=0,1 coincide). Offset intervals have widths a_(k+1)-a_(k), and Gaussian radial independence gives the ratio of half-normal expected order-statistic gaps. For high d, tilting by Gaussian max M_d changes the law by vanishing total variation, as M_d/E M_d ->1 in L1; conditional uniform offset uM_d leaves ell=d-k=d^{1-u²+o_P(1)}, and first-order faces f_j ~ [2^(j+1)/(j+1)!] ell d^(j+1). Simultaneous fixed-rank exponent follows. Actual independent exact signed-face enumeration checked 166 (d,k,j) cases for 3<=d<=8; finite checks do not prove the limit.

value.rationale: Motion-invariant affine sections differ essentially from central section laws: their actual random offset governs how many cross-polytope vertices lie above the plane. Explicit positive probabilities for all d-1 attainable face-vectors and a shared random exponent across all fixed ranks provide a natural complete classification and nontrivial geometric-probability limit.

limitations: Invariant Euclidean-motion measure conditional on meeting interior, generic hyperplane; not central/volume-weighted sampling.
Face vector classification, not unique face-lattice classification; no quantitative convergence rate.
